J1.text: App code plus compiler output is 15% of the Solid 2 demo and Hacker News, and 23% of Solid 1 Hacker News and solid-ui. The Solid runtime is 85%, 57%, 51% and 6%.

J2.text: Unused DOM walks cost 26-44 B gzip per app. A hand-written Solid 2 user page is 47 B (7.5%) smaller than the compiler's output.

J3.text: @solidjs/signals is 12.3 of the Solid 2 demo's 17.8 kB. The core read and recompute path calls the async, transition and error-status code, so those ship in every app.

evidence.source: top-level declaration sizes in the demo's signals regions

J4.text: JSX lowering is upstream on both lines: @solidjs/compiler 2.0.0-rc.16 on Solid 2 and babel-preset-solid on Solid 1. The optimizer runs it in renderChunk in chunk mode.

J5.text: T1 (earlier debate): copying @kobalte/core saved 0 B. The copies are refused as copy-props-use 91, copy-call-spread 39, copy-call-ref 25 and copy-shape 70.

P1.text: Solid 1: port the rule that moves component statements into untracked callbacks (<For>/<Index>, <Show>/<Match> with a parameter, render), with runtime tests.

P2.text: Both lines: clean the code JSX lowering leaves in chunk mode. Drop unused DOM walks, turn functions called at once around one element into statements, and read a shared dynamic part once.

estimate.unit: % of app code, 26-47 B per page measured

P3.text: Both lines: inline a component when its call site passes a spread or a ref, using Solid's mergeProps in the output (roadmap item 2 step 3). This is the only lever that reaches Kobalte and the icon wrappers.

P4.text: Solid 2: runtime feature flags. Solid ships flags for async, transitions and error boundaries, and the optimizer sets them off when the app provably does not use the feature.

P5.text: Solid 2: roadmap item 1 step 3. Wrap statements of a component in a <Show> child or fallback in untrack(() => ...), when the estimate says it is smaller.

A1.text: Fix the lowering leftovers of P2 upstream, in @solidjs/compiler and dom-expressions, so every Solid app gets them, not only optimizer users.

O1.text: P2 rewrites output of an upstream compiler after the fact. Every lowering change upstream can break the pattern match, and module mode (hydrating, server) would not get it.

O2.text: P3 is unmeasured, and T1 shows props-use refusals (91) outnumber spread (39) and ref (25) refusals on Kobalte. Fixing spreads alone leaves most Kobalte copies refused. Roadmap item 2 also says chunk-mode passes do not know mergeProps' local name.

O3.text: P4 needs a design change in @solidjs/signals, which is at 2.0.0-rc.16. Its timeline is not in this repo's control, so it cannot gate a 0.5.0 release.

O4.text: P1 and P5 are each worth tens of bytes. The same rule moved the Solid 2 demo by 12 B, and the demo's Home in a fallback is one call.

evidence.source: roadmap.md item 1 results; debates/v0.5.0 O1, O2
